question: Should Slack intentionally suppress typed automatic tool-progress output when it cannot safely react to a thread target, rather than fall back to a visible Slack message?
rationale: This is an intentional user-visible delivery policy that can hide operational output; tests can verify implementation but cannot select the desired Slack product behavior.

options.title: Approve fail-closed progress policy
options.body: Keep suppression for typed automatic progress without a usable reaction target after current-head full-path Slack proof demonstrates that completed, failed, verbose, and semantic replies remain visible.

options.title: Preserve visible fallback
options.body: Require the Slack path to post a visible message when no reaction target is available, accepting extra progress chrome to avoid suppressing any automatic output.

recommendation.title: Approve fail-closed progress policy
recommendation.body: Keep suppression for typed automatic progress without a usable reaction target after current-head full-path Slack proof demonstrates that completed, failed, verbose, and semantic replies remain visible.
